summary:
## cat=5 warehouse/economy reply model (Hero3 client.bin)

**Dispatch (fo 0x57394):** prologue computes `CTX = fn_0x14ad10() + 0xa3ac` (warehouse context; stored [r7-0xc]) and `M = *node+8` (message struct; [r7-0x10]). Index = `op-3`, bound `<=0x3f`, jump via table @ fo 0xa978c. **Body is read by FIXED byte offsets from M**, NOT via a cursor reader: `M+0xa = payload[2] = body[0]`, `M+0xb = body[1]`, ... Copies use `memcpy = fn_0x19f624(dst,src,len)`; clears use `memset = fn_0x19fb78(dst,val,len)`. The `M[2]` read-cursor is zeroed on dispatch entry but **cat5 ignores it** — every field is a hard-coded offset. All multi-byte values are **LITTLE-ENDIAN** (raw memcpy then native ldrh/ldr; TX `put_u32@0x7e1c4` also writes LE with no byteswap). Common epilogue/return = fo 0x58172. Ops 0x07–0x13,0x15–0x3c all map to the default = 0x58172 (no-op return → server need not reply).

**CTX warehouse layout (offsets from CTX):**
- `+0x2f8` u32 gold balance (0xbe<<2)
- `+0x304` u32, `+0x308` u32 economy counters (0xc1<<2 / 0xc2<<2)
- `+0x1a4`,`+0x1a5` u8 header bytes; `+0x1a6` u16 warehouse item count (0xd3<<1)
- `+0x1a8` 16-byte per-slot flag array (0xd4<<1, memset 0x10)
- `+0x1b8` warehouse item list = 16 × 20-byte rows = 0x140 bytes (0xdc<<1)
- `+0x30c` u16 cash-item count (0xc3<<2); `+0x30e` 16-byte cash flag array
- `+0x320` cash/money item list = 16 × 20-byte rows = 0x140 bytes (0xc8<<2)

**Two reply shapes:** (A) LIST replies (op 0x03/0x3d warehouse, op 0x3f cash) = header + u16 count N + N rows of **21 bytes** (1 flag byte → flag array, 20-byte item → list array; N capped at 16). (B) scalar/ack replies (op 0x14 gold u32; op 0x3e dual-currency; op 0x04 single 23-byte item; op 0x05/0x06/0x40/0x41/0x42 = 1 status byte, nonzero→success which triggers a follow-up TX + list refresh, zero→error UI).

**20-byte item record (row[1..20] of list replies, and op 0x04 body):** `+8`=u8 item category, `+9`=u8 item id (HIGH — consumer `insert@0x176b44` reads [8],[9] then item-lookup `0x14f358`); `+0..7`=two u32 instance words, `+0xa`=u8, `+0xb`=u8, `+0xc..0xf`=i32 (-1 sentinel), `+0x10..0x13`=4×u8 option/enhance bytes (MED, from upload TX struct symmetry @ op 0x41 build 0x57726-0x578f8).

reply_formats.layout: body @ payload[2]: p[2..5] = u32 LE gold. Total body = 4 bytes. (fo 0x57636: memcpy(CTX+0x2f8, M+0xa, 4))
reply_formats.effect: Writes gold into CTX+0x2f8; then AUTO-SENDS a cat5 op 0x3f request (12-byte body, carrying CTX[0x308]) to fetch cash-item list. Server should follow a 0x14 reply by being ready for an inbound 0x3f.

reply_formats.layout: p[2]=u8 →CTX[0x1a5]; p[3]=u8 →CTX[0x1a4]; p[4..5]=u16 LE count N →CTX[0x1a6]; then N rows @ p[6 + i*21]: row[0]=u8 →CTX[0x1a8+i] (slot flag), row[1..20]=20-byte item →CTX[0x1b8 + i*20]. N must be ≤16. Body len = 4 + 21*N. (fo 0x57400 header; loop 0x57528: memcpy 1B @ M+0xe+i*21, 20B @ M+0xf+i*21). Clamp: CTX[0x1a5]=min(CTX[0x1a4],CTX[0x1a5]).
reply_formats.effect: Rebuilds the full warehouse grid (clears CTX+0x1b8 then fills N items). p[2]/p[3] are max-slots/used-count (MED). Tail refreshes UI when CTX[0x38]==3.

reply_formats.layout: p[2]=u8 →CTX[0x1a4]; p[3..4]=u16 LE count N →CTX[0x1a6]; then N rows @ p[5 + i*21]: row[0]=u8 →CTX[0x1a8+i], row[1..20]=20-byte item →CTX[0x1b8 + i*20]. N ≤16. Body len = 3 + 21*N. (fo 0x57c0c; loop 0x57d08: 1B @ M+0xd+i*21, 20B @ M+0xe+i*21).
reply_formats.effect: Same warehouse item array as op 0x3d but 3-byte header (no CTX[0x1a5] byte). Used for initial warehouse open. Tail: UI via fn_0x175b98(global[sl+0x4b0],7,1,1).

reply_formats.layout: p[2..5]=u32 LE →CTX[0x308]; p[6..9]=u32 LE →CTX[0x304]; p[10..11]=u16 LE count N →CTX[0x30c]; then N rows @ p[12 + i*21]: row[0]=u8 →CTX[0x30e+i], row[1..20]=20-byte item →CTX[0x320 + i*20]. N ≤16. Body len = 10 + 21*N. (fo 0x57a00; loop 0x57b2c: 1B @ M+0x14+i*21, 20B @ M+0x15+i*21). Clamp CTX[0x308]=min(CTX[0x308],N).
reply_formats.effect: Fills the cash/money-shop item array at CTX+0x320. Two u32 headers = cash counters (MED). Tail sets CTX[0x38]=3, CTX[0x40]=0 and refreshes UI.

reply_formats.layout: p[2..3]=u16 LE →local (slot/count, MED); p[4]=u8 →local (flag, MED); p[5..24]=20-byte item record. Total body = 23 bytes. (fo 0x57dbc: memcpy 2B @ M+0xa, 1B @ M+0xc, 20B @ M+0xd).
reply_formats.effect: Inserts the 20-byte item into inventory via fn_0x176b44 (reads item[8]=category, item[9]=id). Then AUTO-SENDS cat5 op 0x3d to refresh warehouse list. Item [8]/[9] = HIGH; header u16/u8 semantics MED.

reply_formats.layout: p[2]=u8 status. Body = 1 byte. (fo 0x57e98: ldrb M+0xa; cmp #0).
reply_formats.effect: status!=0 → success: AUTO-SENDS cat5 op 0x3d (list refresh) + shows dialog global[sl+0x4b8]. status==0 → failure UI path fn_0x175b98(M+0xc,7,1,1).

reply_formats.layout: p[2]=u8 status. Body = 1 byte. (fo 0x576d2: ldrb M+0xa; cmp #0; bne success).
reply_formats.effect: status!=0 → success: client removes the uploaded item from its own inventory (reads local state via fn_0x14ad10 globals 0x9c70/0x9c71/0x9e28), then AUTO-SENDS cat5 op 0x03 with the 20-byte item + CTX[0x1a5] count byte. status==0 → UI path fn_0x175b98(M+0xc,7,1,1). No item data is read from THIS reply's wire.

reply_formats.layout: p[2..5]=u32 LE →CTX+0x2f8 (gold, clamped ≥0); p[6..9]=u32 LE →base+0xcc (2nd currency, clamped ≥0). Body = 8 bytes. (fo 0x57ef4: memcpy 4B @ M+0xa to CTX+0x2f8, 4B @ M+0xe to fn_0x14ad10()+0xcc).
reply_formats.effect: Sets gold and a second player-state currency (base+0xcc; likely cash/event points, MED). Both floored to 0 if negative. UI refresh fn_0x15727c + dialog global[sl+0x4bc].

reply_formats.layout: p[2]=u8 status. Body = 1 byte. (fo 0x57f84: ldrb M+0xa; cmp #0; beq fail).
reply_formats.effect: status!=0 → success: client builds a cat5 op 0x40 request from the previously-received cash item at CTX+0x320+slot*20 (put 8 bytes via 0x17e300 + a word via 0x17e1c4 + status byte) and sends it. status==0 → UI fn_0x175b98(M+0xc,7,1,1).

reply_formats.layout: p[2]=u8 status. Body = 1 byte. (fo 0x58036: ldrb M+0xa; cmp #0; bne success else fail).
reply_formats.effect: status!=0 → success: copies the 20-byte cash item from CTX+0x320+slot*20 into a local and inserts into inventory via fn_0x176b44, then formats a result popup (fn_0x1a42a4) + list refresh. status==0 → UI path. No item data read from THIS reply's wire (item comes from prior op 0x3f list).

reply_formats.layout: p[4..] (M+0xc) passed as a display argument to formatter fn_0x1a42a4; p[2..3] not consumed here. Trailing bytes = result message/struct (EUC-KR text likely). (fo 0x579a0).
reply_formats.effect: Shows combine-result popup from p[4] onward, then AUTO-SENDS cat5 op 0x3d to refresh the warehouse list. Exact trailing format LOW; that op 0x3d list refresh is what actually repopulates items.

claims.statement: Body is parsed by FIXED offsets, not a cursor reader. memcpy=fn_0x19f624(dst,src,len), memset=fn_0x19fb78(dst,val,len). The M[2] cursor is zeroed but unused by cat5.
claims.evidence: Every handler uses `adds r3,#imm` on M ([r7-0x10]) then bl 0x19f624; e.g. fo 0x5745e memcpy(CTX+0x1a5, M+0xa, 1); no read of M[2] anywhere in 0x57400-0x58172.

claims.statement: All multi-byte reply fields are little-endian.
claims.evidence: Reads are raw memcpy then native ldrh/ldr (e.g. fo 0x574fe ldrh count, 0x57644 gold u32); TX put_u32 @ fo 0x7e1c4 stores value to stack then memcpy 4B into TX buf with NO byteswap (0x7e1d6 str r0,[sp]; 0x7e1ea memcpy 4).

claims.statement: Warehouse LIST replies (op 0x03/0x3d) fill CTX+0x1b8 (16×20B item array, memset 0x140) and CTX+0x1a8 (16B flag array); count in CTX+0x1a6 (u16). Rows are 21 bytes: 1 flag byte + 20-byte item.
